name: parallel_histogram_equalization_race
task: This project computes a histogram-equalized version of a synthetic grayscale image, split across multiple translation units: include/matrix.h + src/matrix.cpp (a simple row-major integer matrix and a deterministic random-matrix generator), include/histogram.h + src/histogram.cpp (serial and OpenMP-parallel histogram computation), include/pipeline.h + src/pipeline.cpp (histogram equalization built on top of the histogram module), and src/main.cpp (the profiling entry point). compute_histogram_parallel() in src/histogram.cpp parallelizes the pixel-counting loop with '#pragma omp parallel for', but every thread increments the same shared 'histogram' array with no synchronization or reduction, causing a data race: increments are lost under contention, so the parallel histogram's bin counts (and their sum) do not match the serial reference, and this corrupts equalize_histogram() in src/pipeline.cpp, which calls compute_histogram_parallel() internally. Fix compute_histogram_parallel() so it is race-free and produces results identical to compute_histogram_serial() on the same input, while keeping the pixel-counting loop parallelized with OpenMP (do not simply remove the pragma or serialize the loop; use e.g. per-thread local histograms merged after the parallel region, an OpenMP array reduction, or atomic updates). Do not change any function signature declared in include/histogram.h or include/pipeline.h.
notes: build_command compiles the profiling entry point at build/pipeline (src/main.cpp -> matrix.cpp, histogram.cpp, pipeline.cpp). This binary must be built and then executed via run_command to drive DiscoPoP's instrumentation and produce its dynamic profiling output, including dynamic_dependencies, over the parallel loop in compute_histogram_parallel(). test_command builds and runs a separate correctness harness at build/run_tests (from tests/test_main.cpp); it is independent of the profiling binary and should not be used as the DiscoPoP execution target. Both binaries link the same src/matrix.cpp, src/histogram.cpp, src/pipeline.cpp object files, so no separate CMake/Meson/etc. configuration is required — plain 'make' is sufficient to build, run, and test.
